title: Lateral movement & C2
description:
Tunde: 'The persistence runs every shell. Each run beacons out. We pulled three log sources from the egress firewall and the EDR. The Griot's beacon is in there, in plain sight if you know what to look for — but so are 200+ benign DNS queries, ordinary HTTPS sessions, and a long process tree. Find the beacon, follow it across the three tabs, and read the session marker on the trailing proxy line. Submit that as your flag.'

Amaka: 'Correlate across tabs. The DNS query has to come before the proxy CONNECT (resolver lookup first). The EDR will tell you which process initiated the curl. The marker is on the proxy line.

**Be careful — some of the TRAN tokens you find in this lab are static decoys** (operator placeholders, test fixtures left by the red team during reconstruction). Your flag is HMAC-derived against your intern ID — the recipe every Root Access task uses. Pick the right one.'

In the timeline (task 5) you will be asked to cite the exact timestamp, destination, beacon cadence, and process tree path. Take notes.

Reference: MITRE ATT&CK T1071.001 Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols; T1568 Dynamic Resolution; T1041 Exfiltration Over C2 Channel; CISA AA22-279A (TTP patterns for periodic HTTPS beacons to abuse-block IPs).

widgetConfig.instructions: Three egress / EDR tabs. The beacon emerges only when you correlate across them — DNS query first, then proxy CONNECT to the resolved host, then the EDR process tree showing what initiated it. The proxy line carries the session marker. Trust HMAC-format flags; ignore static decoys.
